title: Something Is Wrong: van and nincs with Problems

sections.title: Naming the problem
sections.content: You already know van ("there is") and nincs ("there isn't") for saying what exists. They're just as useful for problems: Nincs helyünk ("We don't have a seat", literally "our place doesn't exist") and Tele van a vonat ("The train is full") both just describe a state with van/nincs, no new verb needed. A problem itself is simply probléma: Van egy problémánk ("We have a problem").

items.spanish: Sajnos tele van ez a vonat, nincs helyünk.
items.english: Unfortunately this train is full, we don't have a seat.

items.spanish: Van egy problémánk: nincs helyünk ezen a vonaton.
items.english: We have a problem: we don't have a seat on this train.

sections.content: tele ("full") behaves like any adjective with van/nincs — Tele van, not Van tele — the same order as Éhes vagyok back in Unit 24 of A1.
